metaphor.shop_equivalent: A glued joint that looked sound but was never load-tested.
metaphor.reason: A passing check that cannot fail maps to an untested joint.

title: The Joint That Never Held

panels.prompt: Foreman admires a freshly glued joint at the bench

lines.speaker: Foreman
lines.text: Glue has set and the clamps are off. This joint looks perfect, so let us ship it today.

lines.speaker: Gauge
lines.text: Did anyone actually load it, or did we only look at it? Looking is not the same as testing.

panels.prompt: The joint snaps the moment weight is put on it

lines.speaker: Gauge
lines.text: There it goes. Every check we ran said it was fine, and still it broke.

lines.speaker: Foreman
lines.text: Then those checks were never really looking at the joint at all, were they?

panels.prompt: A blade guard character rolls in with a scrap board

lines.speaker: Teeth
lines.text: Hello. I am Teeth, and I have one rule. Break the work on purpose, then watch what your check does about it.

panels.prompt: Teeth snaps a scrap board and the alarm finally rings

lines.speaker: Teeth
lines.text: Hear that? The alarm rang, so now the alarm means something.

lines.speaker: Gauge
lines.text: So a green light only counts if a red light was possible.

panels.prompt: The rebuilt joint holds; the crew nods at the bench

lines.speaker: Foreman
lines.text: Next time we break it before we bless it, and only then do we sign off the joint.

arrival_prompt: Teeth rolls into the shop and taps a scrap board against its blade
